metadata.title: Ohmie Build Guide

blocks.text: Two games for an Arduino Uno R3, a 2.42″ OLED, a slide
potentiometer and a buzzer — wired once, flashed from a single
repo. Everything here has been compiled and checked against the

RESIST — Ohmie is a resistor, so he does a resistor’s job. Current streams down a wire at him and your
fader is his resistance. Resist too little and the current sweeps him off the wire; resist too much and
P = I²R cooks him. You ride the gap between the two.
Flappy Ohm — the fader is Ohmie’s height, and you fly him through a field of resistors. No tapping; you
Both run on identical wiring, so you build the hardware once.

Arduino Uno R3
Genuine or clone. Clones often report an unusual USB vendor ID, which only
means you pass the board type explicitly — covered in section 7.

2.42″ OLED, 128×64
SSD1309 controller, 7 pins (GND, VCC, SCK, SDA, RES, DC, CS). SSD1306
panels also work with a one-line change.

Slide pot module
Dual gang, 6 pins as two 3-pin headers: GND, VCC, WIPER per gang. A bare

Buzzer module
3 pins: GND, VCC, SIGNAL. A bare 2-pin buzzer works too — see the note in

Jumper wires
13 male-to-female, or male-to-male plus a breadboard.

USB cable
Type-B for a classic Uno.
The sketches use tone() , which sweeps pitch only on a passive buzzer. Many 3-pin modules carry an active one,
which has its own oscillator and will sound at a single fixed pitch no matter what the sketch asks for. Both are safe to
wire exactly the same way, and section 6 tells you which you have.

69 × 42 mm · SCK=D0, SDA=D1 · SSD1309
SLIDE POT MODULE
75 × 28 mm · dual gang

10 mm
drawn to scale · 2.54 mm pitch · header positions representative
Boards drawn to true relative scale · 2.54 mm header pitch · 4.06 mm across the Uno’s digital headers
Leave gang B of the pot unconnected — one gang is all the game reads. If you have a bare 2-pin buzzer
instead of a module, it’s simply + → D7 and − → GND .
D13 AND D11 CANNOT BE MOVED
They are wired to the ATmega328P’s SPI hardware in silicon. Put the clock on any other pin and the screen simply
stays black. If D13 is genuinely unavailable, switch to I²C ( OLED_BUS 0 , SCL→A5, SDA→A4) rather than software SPI
— software SPI is bit-banged and far too slow to look good.
D12 is MISO. While SPI is enabled in master mode the chip forces that pin to be an input, so anything you drive there is
silently swallowed. The sketches refuse to compile if you put the buzzer on D11, D12 or D13.
Check what your OLED module says about VCC, on the silkscreen or in the listing you bought it from.
Marked 3.3–5 V — the common case. Wire VCC to the Uno’s 5 V pin and carry on.
Marked 3.3 V only — run VCC from the Uno’s 3.3 V pin and put a 1 kΩ resistor in series with each of the five
signal lines (SCK, SDA, RES, DC, CS). Uno logic is 5 V and will otherwise stress a 3.3 V-only panel.
Then check the rest before applying power: nothing bridging 5 V to GND, the pot’s two outer pins on 5 V
and GND with the wiper on A0, and no wire in D0 or D1 — those are the USB serial pins and anything on
You need two things: a compiler for AVR boards, and the U8g2 display library. Pick either route.
Route A — Arduino CLI (what this guide uses)

arduino-cli config init
arduino-cli core update-index
1. Install the Arduino IDE from arduino.cc/en/software.
2. Tools → Board → Arduino AVR Boards → Arduino Uno.
3. Tools → Manage Libraries, search U8g2 by oliver, install.
4. Open the .ino you want and press Upload.
No Git installed? Open github.com/jinglebells2020/flappy-ohmie in a browser, press Code →

Resist/
The current-fighting game. Start here.

PinCheck/
Confirms the pot and buzzer before you load a game.

wiring-bench.html
Interactive wiring builder. Open it in any browser, drag boards, run cables, export

wiring-diagram.svg
The schematic on the previous page.
Each sketch lives in a folder matching its filename, which is what the Arduino toolchain expects. Point
the compiler at the folder, not the .ino .
Do this before loading a game. It needs only the pot and buzzer wired — no OLED — and it tells you in
seconds whether your slider sweeps properly and which kind of buzzer you have.
You’re looking for something like /dev/cu.usbmodem101 on macOS, /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux, or COM3

WHAT YOU SEE
WHAT IT MEANS
Bar sweeps the full width, buzzer pitch
Both parts are good. Move on to section 7.

Number never moves
A0 is on an end pin, not the wiper. Swap A0 with one of the other two.
5 V and GND are on the wrong pins, or you picked pins from two different

Stops short, e.g. 40–980
Normal for a cheap fader. Widen POT_LO / POT_HI in the game sketch

Buzzer beeps but the pitch never changes
You have an active buzzer. Harmless — the games still sound, just at one

Silent
Check polarity, and that SIGNAL is on D7 and VCC has 5 V.
A serial monitor holds the port, and the uploader cannot reset the board through a port something else owns. This is
the single most common cause of programmer is not responding .
Wire the OLED now as well, then:
Sketch uses 21094 bytes (65%) of program storage space.
Global variables use 1555 bytes (75%) of dynamic memory,
Low memory available, stability problems may occur.
1 KB of the RAM is the display framebuffer, and U8g2 links in another 96 bytes of I²C buffers even on SPI. Peak stack
for these sketches is around 200 bytes, so there is roughly 2× headroom. Nothing is wrong.
Swap Resist for FlappyOhm to load the other game. Always pass --fqbn arduino:avr:uno explicitly
— many Uno clones report a USB vendor ID the tooling doesn’t recognise, so auto-detection reports the
board as Unknown even though it is a perfectly ordinary ATmega328P.
Uploading from the Arduino IDE instead? Open Resist/Resist.ino , pick Arduino Uno and your port
Current I streams at Ohmie from the right. Your slider sets his resistance R .
I > R — the current wins and shoves him downstream. Off the left edge and you are SWEPT AWAY.
P = I²R — resisting is work, and work is heat. He glows from the inside; fill the heat bar and you BURN OUT.
The notch on the R bar marks where R = I , the point where he holds his ground. During a surge that
notch is also exactly where he cooks fastest, so you have to give ground, cool off, and take it back in the
lull. That push-and-recover rhythm is the whole game.
Surges get stronger and arrive sooner, and the ramp never plateaus — so every run ends, and skill
decides when. Simulated against the real physics:

Never really move the fader
swept at ~11 s

Slam it to maximum and leave it
burned out at ~35 s

Match R to I, ignore the heat
burned out at ~40 s

Match I, back off when hot
43–55 s
Slide the fader to start, and again to retry after a crash. Your best score is kept in EEPROM and survives
Your slider position is Ohmie’s height, with a little spring so he glides rather than snaps. Thread the
resistors. Every one cleared is a point, a rising blip and a ring pop.
Difficulty ramps: the world speeds up and the gap tightens from 30 px to 21 px. Collision uses a 9×9 box
at his centre, so his feet and antenna pass through harmlessly — deliberately forgiving, because near-
Every gap the generator can produce was checked for a reachable centre. The tightest window in the

whole difficulty curve is 10 px, and the spring closes the worst 22 px jump to within 0.04 px in the time
available at top speed. It is always physically possible — reaction time is the only limit.
A serial monitor is holding the port. Close it and retry. If it persists, press
reset on the Uno just as the upload starts.

Screen totally black
Clock must be on D13 under hardware SPI. Then try OLED_SSD1309 0
— wrong controller is the most common cause. Then check RES/DC/CS

Ohmie moves the wrong way
SLIDER_FLIP 1 , or swap the pot’s 5 V and GND ends.

Can’t reach the very top or bottom
Widen POT_LO / POT_HI — try 0 and 1023.

Ohmie jitters when you hold still
Noisy fader. Add a 100 nF capacitor from A0 to GND.

Motion looks choppy
Set SHOW_FPS 1 ; the title screen prints render time. Over 20 ms means
the bus is the bottleneck — get onto OLED_BUS 1 .

Garbage or tearing
You’re on I²C with a long cable. Shorten it or move to SPI.

No sound at all
Check SIGNAL is on D7 and the module has 5 V and GND. A 2-pin buzzer

Board type not detected
Normal on clones. Always pass --fqbn arduino:avr:uno and -p
Working as intended — you put the buzzer on D11, D12 or D13. Use D2–
Every setting worth touching sits at the top of each sketch.

OLED_BUS
1 hardware SPI (~50 fps, the default), 0 I²C (~30 fps), 2 software SPI

OLED_SSD1309
1 for a 2.42″ SSD1309 panel, 0 for SSD1306.

SHOW_FPS
Prints render time on the title screen.

PIN_BUZZ
Buzzer pin. D2–D7 are free; D7 keeps the wiring at one end of the header.

OHM_R
Ohmie’s size. Everything else scales from it — he is drawn from primitives, not a
DRIFT is how hard the current shoves, HEAT_GAIN and HEAT_COOL set how fast he cooks and
recovers. Sustainable power is HEAT_COOL / HEAT_GAIN — raise it and the game gets forgiving, lower it
GAP_START and GAP_MIN are the gap heights, and the speed line sets the ramp. If you change
OHM_R , OHM_HIT or GAP_MIN , re-check that every gap is still reachable rather than trusting your eye —
a hitbox that no longer fits produces gaps that cannot be passed at all.

5V
OLED VCC, pot VCC, buzzer VCC
Three wires share this pin.

GND
OLED GND, pot GND, buzzer GND
The Uno has three GND pins; spread the load.

A0
Pot WIPER A
The only analog read in either game.

D7
Buzzer SIGNAL
Any of D2–D7 works.

D8
OLED RES
Ordinary GPIO, reassignable.

D9
OLED DC
Ordinary GPIO, reassignable.

D10
OLED CS
Ordinary GPIO, reassignable.

D11
OLED SDA / MOSI
Fixed by SPI hardware.

D12
—
MISO. Forced to an input by SPI; unusable as an output.

D13
OLED SCK / D0
Fixed by SPI hardware.

D0 / D1
—
USB serial. Leave empty or uploads break.

PinCheck — 4046 B flash (12%), 1839 B RAM free
